notes: The frozen capability list (draft §15.2 condition 1). A capability exists here only after it
has been *frozen*: a name, the CLI entry it answers, the shape of its request/response, its
side-effect ceiling and its scope semantics. The whitelist then says how to *recognise* such an
object; this file says the capability is allowed to exist at all.
`kind` decides the routing default in `airoot scope decide` (draft §12.1): `tool` means a
single-file general-purpose CLI whose answer is always the same (never asks), `runtime` means
an interpreter environment where project-vs-data-root is a real choice (asks).
`side_effects` is a ceiling from the published sideEffect enum: a candidate object may not
Growth path (draft §15.4): propose -> freeze here -> add a whitelist evidence predicate -> only
then can discover/adopt see it. Never hard-code a directory name instead.
cap-2 (draft §82, decision D9): `media_probe` was unfrozen. Freezing a name is what lets
`discover`/`adopt`/`capability check` speak about it, and that name appeared in **no**
agent-facing document and had no trusted source — an unexplained name is a name an account
cannot interpret. It can come back through the growth path above once something needs it.

capabilities.notes: any CPython-compatible interpreter directory; a project venv is the project case
one object may host several versions (nvm); the active one is observed, not chosen
JDK or JRE; the home is derived from where the entrypoint was found
never a bundled mingit inside another object: the predicate requires depth <= 2 and shallowest wins
a build tool is the classic machine-level generic CLI
P1 simulation only: the payload is data and is never executed (docs/schema/README.md)
